newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's oldest woman celebrates 126th birthday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's oldest woman celebrates 126th birthday.

text.p: Former slave Maria do Carmo Geronimo, Brazil's oldest woman and possibly the oldest person in the world, celebrated her 126th birthday on Wednesday.
"My secret in life is this -- to sing," Geronimo said at a birthday party held for her in Sao Paulo. Despite her age, she walks unassisted and is in generally good health.

On Wednesday night, she was to attend a concert by popular singer Roberto Carlos, known in Brazil as "The King," local Globo television said. Carlos has promised to meet Geronimo, fulfilling one of her dreams.

As a slave, Geronimo did not have the right to a birth certificate when she was born on March 5, 1871. But the Brazilian Guinness Book of Records has recognised her baptism certificate as proof that she is the oldest person in the country.

The international edition still recognises Frenchwoman Jeanne Calment, who has a birth certificate, as the world's oldest person. Calment, who is wheelchair-bound and blind, celebrated her 122nd birthday on Feb. 21.
